newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola, Zaire rebels in joint exercise--sources.
newsitem.headline: Angola, Zaire rebels in joint exercise--sources.

text.p: The Angolan army and Zairean rebels are performing joint military exercises on the Angolan side of the border between the two countries, expatriate mining sources said on Friday.
One source said the exercises were taking place near the border town of Dundo, where Rwandan refugees have been crossing into Angola's diamond-rich area, from Zaire, the country's northern neighbour.

"Our people in Dundo sent a report this morning that confirms that the Zairean rebels and the FAA (Angolan Armed Forces) are carrying out joint military exercises on the border," the source told Reuters.
"They are not trying to hide it either," he added.
The Angolan army sent tanks and heavy artillery to the area during the week, the source said. "They are practising live fire exercises. They are doing very basic ground manoeuvres."
A Western diplomat in Luanda told Reuters that Angolan army chief Joao de Matos was in Dundo on Friday and had made several trips between the town and the capital Luanda over the past two weeks.
Angolan national radio reported on Wednesday the government had tightened control on its side of the border after increased numbers of Zaireans had crossed to flee the conflict in their homeland.
Angola's former rebel movement UNITA also said on Friday more than 500 Rwandan refugees crossed the border into areas it controls in Lunda Norte this week.

"At least 500 of these Rwandans crossed over a few days ago...at Nzage," UNITA's chief negotiator in the Angolan peace process, Isaias Samakuva, told Reuters. "From my point of view it is a humanitarian situation. I think we would have to help these people."
Despite a 1994 peace accord between the Angolan government and UNITA, who fought a 20-year civil war, vast areas still fall under the control of the rival sides.
Angola has vast diamond riches in the Lunda Norte and Lunda Sul provinces where the refugees are crossing and most of the area is controlled by UNITA.
The region has been extremely volatile, with UNITA and the government wrestling for the diamond wealth. Dundo is one of the few areas in the region under government control.

Another expatriate diamond mining official, who operates close to the town, said there were a "good number" of Rwandan refugees crossing the border. He said more Angolan soldiers and police had been sent but were unable to stop refugees.

The U.N. refugee agency said earlier this month it had unconfirmed reports of 30,000 Rwandans in Zaire heading for the Angolan border, fleeing Zaire's rebels fighting to overthrow President Mobutu Sese Seko.
The rebels have taken control of over half of Zaire since they launched their military campaign last October.
